description.text: works behind a worn wooden counter. Shelves of packaged goods recede into soft shadow on both sides, and warm practical light from a shaded pendant falls across the countertop, picking out the grain, a few crumbs and the damp streak left by the cloth. A chipped ceramic mug and a small stack of receipts sit near the register. He finishes wiping the surface in a broad, practiced arc, folds the cloth once and sets it down beside the register. His posture is unhurried; he checks the counter, then lifts his gaze toward the customer standing beyond the frame. His shoulders settle and his expression stays reserved, mouth relaxed, eyes steady. When he answers, the delivery is flat and close, with little warmth or emphasis, the kind of dry, near-microphone speech that sits just above the room tone. Dust motes drift in the warm light, which has a slight amber cast, and the shadows under the shelves are deep and brown. The surrounding shop is quiet: a low electrical hum, the faint tick of the register, the soft settle of the cloth. He keeps one hand resting on the counter edge as he speaks, then lets the silence return after the last word.
